title: Console IA for Security → Audit Export (destinations list, create flow, detail/health states)
creator: Tessa Morgan
description:
Goal
Define the Console information architecture (IA) and core page structure for SIEM-ready audit export beta under Console navigation: Security → Audit Export.

This ticket covers:
- Destinations list page (empty, populated, error states)
- Create destination flow (type selection, credentials, filters, test delivery, confirmation)
- Destination detail page, including health/status visualization and common troubleshooting affordances

Out of scope
- Final visual design system polish (handled in follow-up UI tickets)
- Copywriting/legal disclaimers finalization (Docs/Legal review in parallel)
- Advanced features beyond beta (multi-sink fanout policies, vendor-specific field mapping, historical bulk backfill UI)

Primary users
- Security admins / platform admins in enterprise customers (Hosted, Dedicated, Private) who need audit events in Splunk/Datadog/S3.

Constraints/requirements (from PRD + eng)
- Feature must be behind a per-tenant beta feature flag.
- Export is at-least-once; UI must not imply exactly-once delivery.
- Destinations can be paused/disabled; failures must be visible and actionable.
- Filtering is a core cost-control lever; UI must support safe defaults and validation guidance.
- Health information is sourced from control plane API fields (e.g., last_success_at, last_error, backlog_estimate) and should degrade gracefully if unavailable.

Deliverables
1) IA map + navigation placement
- Add new nav item: Security → Audit Export (beta badge while flagged)
- Entry point visible only if feature flag is enabled AND user has permission to manage audit export.

2) Page-level flows
A) Destination list
- Empty state: explain what Audit Export is + supported destinations (Splunk HEC, Datadog Logs, S3) + CTA “Create destination”
- Populated state: table of destinations (Name, Type, Status/Health, Last delivered, Backlog estimate, Updated by/Updated at)
- Row actions: View details, Pause/Resume, Disable (with confirmation), Delete (if allowed), “Send test event” shortcut (optional based on ENG feasibility)
- Inline banner: “Duplicates possible (at-least-once). Recommended dedupe key: event_id + destination_id + emitted_at.” (wording to be finalized w/ Security)

B) Create destination flow (wizard)
Step 0: Destination type selection
- Splunk HEC | Datadog Logs | S3
- Show short requirements per type (e.g., Splunk HEC URL/token, Datadog region/site + API key, S3 bucket/prefix + KMS)

Step 1: Basics
- Destination name (required)
- Environment scope (if applicable): Production / Staging (must align to backend model)

Step 2: Credentials & endpoint
- Type-specific fields with validation + secure-input behavior (never re-display secret after save)
- Provide “Rotate credentials” guidance link (goes to docs)
- Error handling design: show error_id for support; classify auth vs network vs throttling when known

Step 3: Filters
- Include/exclude by event type
- Actor/resource/environment fields as available in beta
- UX requirement: prevent user from accidentally filtering out critical security events (suggested presets + warning)
- Provide “Preview matching events” as future enhancement; for beta, provide clear examples and a link to schema v1

Step 4: Test delivery
- Button “Send test event” (creates a synthetic event) and show result (success, pending, failed) with timestamp
- If test fails, user can either fix config or “Save anyway (not recommended)” depending on PM/Eng decision

Step 5: Review & create
- Summary of config (redacting secrets)
- Final acknowledgment: at-least-once semantics + duplicates possible; responsibility for sink-side dedupe

C) Destination detail page
- Header: Destination name + type + status pill
- Tabs (recommended): Overview | Filters | Delivery settings (if any) | Activity
- Health widget:
  - Current state: Healthy / Degraded / Paused / Disabled
  - Last delivered at
  - Backlog estimate (with “unknown” state)
  - Last error (collapsed by default; expand shows error details + error_id)
  - Actions: Pause/Resume, Send test event, View logs (if we have link), Replay (if enabled later)
- Troubleshooting panel:
  - Common errors by connector: 401/403 token, 429 rate limits, 5xx, schema rejection
  - Link to runbook + setup guide
- Activity (audit trail of config changes): “Created by”, “Updated by”, “Paused by” etc. (depends on backend audit log coverage)

Health & status state definitions (for UI)
- Healthy: no recent errors, last_success_at within expected window, backlog within normal bounds
- Degraded: recent errors OR growing backlog above threshold; show guidance “Check credentials / throttle / destination availability”
- Paused: user-initiated pause; no delivery attempts; show resume CTA
- Disabled: destination disabled (beta gating/offboarding); show re-enable path (if allowed)
- Unknown: service not reporting; show neutral state and link to status docs

Open questions
- Do we allow Delete for beta? If yes, what happens to buffered events? (Need PM/Eng alignment)
- Do we expose ‘Replay time window’ in beta UI or keep it operator-only? (ENG-13934 suggests operator tooling first)
- How do we represent per-sink partial failures (e.g., some batches fail) without overwhelming users? Proposal: show last error + counts over last hour, keep detailed metrics in dashboards.

Links
- PRD: Confluence “SIEM-ready audit export (beta) PRD”
- Design spec: Confluence “Audit export filtering and delivery guarantees”
- Related eng: ENG-13930 (Console UI), ENG-13929 (Console backend), ENG-13928 (health endpoints)

Acceptance criteria
- IA and page outlines reviewed by Console Eng (Chloe Martin / Felix Schneider) and Security Eng (Marcus Lin / Kevin Osei).
- Documented list of UI states + required API fields for each screen.
- Wireframes delivered covering list, create wizard, and detail with health states.
- Copy placeholders included for dedupe/disclaimer messaging and permissions/feature-flag gating.
comments: 2025-02-06 — Chloe Martin: Please make sure the list page is usable even when health endpoints are lagging (show 'Unknown' rather than blocking rendering). Also call out required API fields explicitly so we can align with ENG-13928.
2025-02-07 — Marcus Lin: +1 on not implying exactly-once. Also we need a clear permission boundary: viewers can see destination health but cannot view/edit secrets. Add to IA notes.

2025-02-10 — Felix Schneider: Backend can provide: destination_id, name, type, state (enabled/paused/disabled/degraded), last_success_at, last_attempt_at, last_error_code, last_error_message (sanitized), last_error_id, backlog_estimate. We likely won’t have per-hour counters at launch.

2025-02-12 — Naomi Feldman: For beta, allow Create/Update/Pause/Resume; Delete only for internal unless we’re confident about buffering semantics. Please design delete as hidden/guarded action with a ‘contact support’ pattern for now.

2025-02-14 — Tessa Morgan: Posted v1 wireframes with: list + empty state, 5-step create wizard, and detail page with health widget + troubleshooting panel. Added state matrix and copy placeholders for at-least-once/dupes.

2025-02-18 — Kevin Osei: In troubleshooting, add explicit guidance: dedupe by audit_event.event_id (schema v1) and sink-specific recommendations (e.g., Splunk index-time vs search-time). Also ensure test event is clearly labeled synthetic and includes tenant/workspace fields.

2025-02-24 — Tessa Morgan: Updated wireframes: permissions note (no secret readback), delete action moved behind 'Contact support', and added 'Unknown' health state. Ready for handoff to ENG-13930 + DES-612/613.
2025-03-03 — Chloe Martin: Handoff complete. We’ll implement wizard + list first; detail page troubleshooting panel may ship as a collapsed section if time-constrained.
